summary: Terminal SSE marker suppressed after edge multiplexed-priority rewrite during bursty requests
description:
Issue summary:

Customer ClearMind Analytics reports that several long-running SSE conversations intermittently terminate without the final '\n--end\n' terminal marker. The streamed text appears complete to the model engine and worker, but the client never receives the terminal event that signifies the completion of the response payload.

Impact:
- Affects a subset of dedicated customers on prod-us-east behind our edge multiplexing proxy during bursty traffic (high concurrent SSE sessions).
- Symptoms reported as 'incomplete message' by the customer's ingestion service; downstream pipeline waits for end marker and times out, causing duplicate retry traffic.
- Multiple sessions observed over a 3-hour window; customer reported increased error rate and higher request latency and retries.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: pool-id ded-us-east-7
- Edge: http multiplexing / priority-rewrite enabled (edge config v2026-02-28)
- Client: ClearMind ingestion service using SSE with chunked JSON events, keepalive enabled every 25s
- Models used: open-llama-13b-v2 (pinned), inference-config: streaming=true, chunk_size=1024, heartbeat=25s

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1. Start 250 concurrent SSE sessions from ClearMind's ingestion fleet to the Redwood endpoint (region us-east).
2. Send prompt that triggers 12–18s model generation with 3–5 chunked events plus final '\n--end\n' marker.
3. Under burst, 1–3% of sessions do not receive the final marker and hang until client-side timeout.

Expected behavior:
- The final terminal marker and metadata event that signals completion should always be delivered to the client, even under edge priority rewrites.

Actual behavior:
- Final terminal marker is not delivered to the client in affected sessions. Server-side worker logs indicate generation finished and final event queued; trace through the gateway shows the final frame was emitted but may have been dropped or suppressed between the gateway and the edge proxy multiplexing layer.

Logs / traces / evidence:
- Customer provided sample session id: session-20260310-ck82a
- Edge trace (gateway request-id: gw-9a2c): shows final frame emitted at 2026-03-10T14:12:47.342Z
- Edge-proxy logs (edge-node e-11): last activity for stream shows priority-rewrite flush at 2026-03-10T14:12:47.350Z with no outgoing write logged for the terminal marker.
- Worker logs: worker-93 wrote final_event for session-20260310-ck82a at 2026-03-10T14:12:47.341Z, acked by gateway.
- Customer nginx front of their ingestion cluster shows open connection with no additional bytes past 14:12:47.350Z and eventual client timeout at 14:13:17Z.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable edge priority-rewrite (edge config toggle) for the dedicated pool as a mitigation; customer applied and reported reduction in incidents during 30m validation window.

Attachments:
- Link to gzipped trace bundle (S3): s3://redwood-support/evidence/SUP-338777/session-20260310-ck82a-trace.tgz

Notes:
- Issue appears related to concurrency and edge-level prioritization/rewriting where multiplexed streams are reordered for resource fairness. Not every session is impacted; likely race between final flush and proxy multiplex reorder/eviction path.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:08 — Aisha Malik (Support): Acknowledged with customer, collected traces and asked for low-traffic test window. Provided mitigation to toggle edge priority-rewrite. Assigned to Riley for deeper investigation.

2026-03-10 17:22 — Riley Chen (SRE): Reproduced locally with stress harness (250 concurrent SSEs) against edge-staging. Observed ~1.8% missing terminal markers when priority-rewrite emulation is enabled. Captured pcap and proxy logs. Linking artifacts to GH issue for a telemetry fix.

2026-03-11 09:41 — Jonah Park (Runtime): Reviewed worker and gateway traces. Worker emits event and gateway ack shows write queued. Suspect bug in the edge-proxy multiplexed flush path: when a stream is demoted due to priority rewrite, the terminal control frame may be coalesced with a heartbeat and dropped by a subsequent backpressure path.

2026-03-11 11:05 — Riley Chen (SRE): Created replicable test in k8s using edge-proxy image edge:v2026-02-28 and stress client; reproduced consistently. Filed internal PR to instrument flush path and dump frames on demotion: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4821.

2026-03-12 08:30 — Customer (ClearMind SRE - Diego Alvarez): Applied edge toggle as recommended; incidents dropped to 0 during monitoring window. Requests timeline for patch ETA as they run heavy production traffic.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Priority-rewrite demotion leads to stream being queued in a backpressure buffer that discards zero-length control-only writes when coalesced with keepalive frames.
Hypothesis 2: HTTP/2 multiplexer in edge-proxy has a bug where write completions for demoted streams are not replayed when flush is forced by a final control frame.
Data point: When demotion path is simulated with lower buffer budget, the number of dropped terminal markers increases linearly with concurrency; indicates buffer write-path is implicated.
Telemetry gap: Need an event that records 'control-frame-coalesced' in edge-proxy; added in PR #4821. Also added stream-id mapping to proxy logs for easier correlation.
Repro steps validated in staging using stress harness 1.2: confirmed missing terminal marker only with priority-rewrite enabled; disabling it removes the failure mode.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Customer continues to run with priority-rewrite disabled for ded-us-east-7 (edge toggle).

Fix-in-progress: Internal patch to edge-proxy multiplexed flush and backpressure handling (PR #4821) adds explicit flush-and-replay for control-only writes on demotion. Patch under code review and unit tests added to cover control-frame-only flush scenarios.
Planned rollout: Canary edge-proxy build to be deployed to staging on 2026-03-13, limited rollout to 5% of traffic on prod-us-east on 2026-03-15 if no regressions are observed.

Post-deploy validation: SRE will run stress harness for 2 hours and monitor terminal-marker deliverability metric. Customer will be notified and asked to re-enable priority-rewrite only after 48h of stability.
Follow-ups: Create an alert in Redwood Console for 'terminal-marker-lost' rate exceeding 0.1% for dedicated pools and add a line to the streaming runbook describing the mitigation toggle.
